title: Projective Hom-complex model with its derived evaluation
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $P^\bullet$ a bounded-above cochain complex of projective $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and $N^\bullet$ any cochain complex of $R$-modules. Write $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms into $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $D^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P^\bullet,N^\bullet)$, the product total Hom complex of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], with $d(f)=d_Nf-(-1)^{|f|}fd_P$. Write $-\otimes_R^L-$ for the left derived total tensor product and $R\operatorname{Hom}_R$ for its right adjoint internal Hom. The canonical comparison
$$Q(D^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QP^\bullet,QN^\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism, natural contravariantly in $P^\bullet$ and covariantly in $N^\bullet$. The ordinary direct-sum total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_R D^\bullet)$ represents $QP^\bullet\otimes_R^LQ(D^\bullet)$. Under these comparisons the derived evaluation (the counit for $QP^\bullet\otimes_R^L-\dashv R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QP^\bullet,-)$) is represented by the chain map
$$x\otimes f\longmapsto(-1)^{pq}f(x)\in N^{p+q},\qquad x\in P^p,\quad f\in D^q.$$
Here total tensor has differential $d(x\otimes f)=d_Px\otimes f+(-1)^px\otimes d_Df$. No finite-generation assumption on $P^p$ and no boundedness assumption on $N^\bullet$ are imposed.

proof.text: Because every projective module is flat (lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat), the bounded-above complex P is K-flat by the bounded-above flat-complex theorem (lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat). This uses only the stated upper bound on P; N is arbitrary.

For every integer n, the cohomology of the product-total Hom complex in degree n is the group of homotopy classes of maps P to N[n]: apply the Hom-complex quotient statement (lem-sc-module-hom-complex-quotient) to the shifted target N[n]. Since P is bounded above and termwise projective, the canonical map from homotopy-category maps out of P to derived-category maps is bijective (lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative). The defining derived Hom identity in Tag 0A5W identifies these groups with H^n(RHom_R(QP,QN)); therefore the cohomology maps induced by the canonical comparison Q(D) to RHom are isomorphisms in every degree, so that comparison is an isomorphism. The construction uses only the localization Q and is natural under precomposition in P and postcomposition in N.

source.place: Tags 0A8H, 0A5W and 0A66; equation cohomology-hom-complex and Lemma RHom-out-of-projective

proof.text: The K-flat tensor-model theorem (lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model), applied to the K-flat complex P and the arbitrary complex D, gives a canonical isomorphism Q(Tot(P tensor_R D)) ≅ QP tensor_R^L QD. Thus the ordinary direct-sum total tensor in the statement represents the derived tensor, with its differential d(x tensor f)=d_Px tensor f+(-1)^p x tensor d_Df.

source.place: Tag 06YH, derived tensor computed on a K-flat first complex

proof.text: The chain-level tensor-Hom transpose from Tags 0A5Y and 0GWQ sends a homogeneous tensor x tensor f with x in degree p and f in degree q to (-1)^(pq) f(x). Substituting the Hom differential d_D(f)=d_N f-(-1)^q f d_P and the tensor differential shows that the two sides have matching d_N(f(x)) and f(d_P x) terms with the displayed Koszul signs; hence this is a chain map. Under the comparison of the preceding two steps it is the counit of the derived tensor–RHom adjunction, because the chain map is the ordinary evaluation corresponding to the identity under the Hom–tensor bijection. The calculation is independent of finite generation and of bounds on N.

All comparison maps used above are induced by precomposition, postcomposition, tensoring and the same signed evaluation formula. These operations commute with maps of complexes, so the comparison Q(D) to RHom is contravariantly natural in P and covariantly natural in N, and the represented counit is natural in both variables. The zero complex, a shifted rank-one free module, and an unbounded N give the stated formulas directly; no finite-generation hypothesis enters any step.
